chunks: From him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah and Ali ibn Hadeed, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr al-Kha'thami, from Amr ibn al-Bara', who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, our companions say that if a man divorces his wife once or a hundred times, it is only one divorce. And it had reached us from you and from your fathers that they used to say: if he divorces once or a hundred times, it is only one.' He said: 'It is as it reached you.'
ai.seo_question: Does repeating the word 'divorce' multiple times count as one divorce or multiple divorces in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the prevailing view among the Shia companions that multiple pronouncements of divorce in a single session, regardless of quantity, constitute only one revocable divorce (*talaq wah*). This ruling highlights the distinct Shia jurisprudential position against the majority Sunni view of counting each utterance separately, emphasizing the continuity of the marital bond until the completion of the waiting period (*iddah*).
